Nulla Vitae

Vestibulum id ligula porta felis euismod semper. Sed posuere consectetur est at lobortis. Let us walk the evaluation metrics.

Mean Squared Error averages the squared gaps between predicted and observed values, which makes it sensitive to outliers:

\[ \text{MSE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2 \]

Root Mean Squared Error returns those units to the scale of the target:

\[ \text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2} \]

Mean Absolute Error averages the magnitude of the error while ignoring its direction:

\[ \text{MAE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left| y_i - \hat{y}_i \right| \]

And the coefficient of determination reports the share of variance in the target explained by the features, bounded at one:

\[ R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \bar{y})^2} \]
